Anna L.: quick heads-up — profiling run on a 3090/4090 mix exposed odd kernel routing at seqlen ~1024-2048, throughput drops ~12% when tensor cores are chosen
Miguel: did you repro locally or only on CI trace?
Anna L.: repro'd locally, took perf traces with nvprof and our internal microprof. Looks like kernel selector picks `tensor_core_fp8_bool` path for certain sm compute capability combos even when FP8 throughput is worse for mid seqlen
Dina: hmm. how are we detecting capability today? just reading `cudaGetDeviceProperties` + driver version?
Anna L.: currently: cuDeviceGetAttribute(CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_COMPUTE_CAPABILITY_MAJOR/MINOR) + probe for `supportsTensorCore` via driver reported features. But that doesn't tell us FP8 perf cliff on older SMs.
Kevin: can you paste the short repro command?
Anna L.: sure — run on target card with this tiny harness: ```./infer_bench --model=llama-13b --bs=1..8 --seqlen=256,512,1024,1536,2048 --trace-kernels``` it produces the kernel pick list and timings
Miguel: output looked like?
Anna L.: for SM86 card: picks fp16 fastpath for seqlen<=512, then switches to fp8/kc-tc path at 1024 and that kernel has ~1.12x higher per-token latency at 1536. stack traces point to different matmul kernel selection.
Sasha: is KV cache behavior implicated? maybe bigger KV stride causes l2 thrash for that kernel variant
Anna L.: good call. I inspected KV memory ops: fp8 kernel uses a slightly different tile layout that increased global load count for cached KV pages; at ~1500 tokens we hit a TLB/L2 miss pattern.
Dina: so there are two orthogonal problems: (1) capability detection isn't predictive of perf cliff, (2) kernel selection heuristics don't consider sequence-length-caused cache effects
Kevin: proposals: (A) add a tiny startup microprobe (run 3 short matmuls at a couple seq lengths) to measure real device perf vectors, store in local cache; (B) extend selector to incorporate seqlen heuristic and memory-pressure score; (C) fallback policy to prefer fp16 kernel for SM8x when measured FP8 regression >5%
Anna L.: +1 to microprobe — cheap and effective. I sketched a probe payload in infra: ```probe_keys = [128, 512, 1536]; for k in probe_keys: run_matmul(sample_k=k, bs=1) record throughput``` store result as device profile key: <pciid>-<driver>-<sm>
Miguel: where to keep results? local cache + emitted to console metrics so customers can see device profile?
Dina: store in node agent persistent cache and emit to Redwood Console as `device_probe.v1` metric. Add TTL 24h and invalidate on driver update.
Sasha: need to be careful for private/offline installs — keep probe optional via config flag `device.probe.enabled` default true for hosted and dedicated, false for air-gapped unless admin opts in
DeployBot: rollout plan: canary to 10% nodes with probe + heuristic change, monitor INF-2473, rollback safe flag added
Anna L.: action items: 1) Miguel to add microprobe harness and probe keys (PR) 2) Dina to wire persistence + console metric 3) Kevin to implement selector change and fallback policy 4) Sasha to add config toggle + docs. I'll open INF-2473 and add logs/traces. Anyone object? :thumbsup: / :eyes:  
Kevin: no objections, will start on kernel selector patch tomorrow.
Miguel: I'll prototype the probe and share raw traces in this thread.
Dina: I'll stub the console metric and unit tests.
Sasha: I'll update private deploy docs and config schema.
Anna L.: thanks — tagging INF-2473 and leaving notes with sample traces. If we can land microprobe + fallback quickly we should get that 12% back. :rocket:
